name: Data.nonempty_modulus_places
summary: The chosen place above g0 named by the identity infinite place divides M, hence M^c, hence the modulus.

steps.claim: The chosen place w0 above g0 that chosenEquiv(D, 0) attaches to the identity infinite place divides the modulus mModulus(D, theta, c, b); so the set of places is nonempty.
The ideal of the modulus, M^c X (X = Q or 1), is contained in M^c, and M^c is contained in M because c is nonzero.
M, the product of the chosen places, is contained in the prime w0, one of its factors.
